description: Style taxonomy for authoring new soldier sprites that match the existing 12. Companion to soldiers.json — that file says WHAT each sprite is; this file says which building-blocks are ALLOWED and how they combine. Pick one value per category, feed into promptTemplate, and the result stays visually consistent.

style.framing: Round portrait, bust-up (head + shoulders + shield). Character centered with ~4% circular margin. Transparent corners on the source PNG.
style.background: Transparent. No scene, no environment. Downstream renderer adds the dark disc.
style.lineWork: Bold black outlines, uniform weight, not sketchy.
style.shading: Clean cel-shading with 2–3 value steps per material. No soft airbrush gradients.
style.lighting: Top-left key light, soft ambient fill. Highlights on helm crest and shield boss.
style.resolution: ~1100–1400 px square source raster. Renderer downsamples to 60·DPR (or 120·DPR in high-res mode).
style.aesthetic: Professional esports mascot meets grand-strategy portrait — flat vector silhouettes with painted-metal detailing.

spear.doru: Long hoplite thrusting spear, bronze leaf-blade, wooden shaft.
spear.xyston: Macedonian cavalry lance, double-length, iron butt-spike.
spear.short-spear: One-handed stabbing spear, typical of Persian Immortals.

sword.gladius: Short Roman stabbing sword, wide double-edge blade.
sword.la-tene-longsword: Long iron Celtic slashing sword with anthropomorphic hilt.

polearm.pilum: Roman heavy throwing javelin with soft-iron shank.

ranged.recurve-bow: Persian short recurve with decorated limbs.

beast.tusks: War-elephant ivory tusks, often capped with iron sleeves.

modifiers.dual-wield: Secondary off-hand blade (e.g. samurai wakizashi paired with katana).

spangenhelm.crest: none, riveted iron segments, nasal guard

turban.crest: cloth wrap, sometimes with jewel brooch

bare-lime-spike.crest: no helm — lime-washed auburn hair spiked back like a mane, drooping moustache

heavy.muscle-cuirass: Sculpted bronze or iron breastplate, anatomical.
heavy.lorica-segmentata: Roman banded plate over leather straps.
heavy.o-yoroi-lamellar: Japanese silk-laced iron scales in boxy cuirass.

medium.scale-mail: Overlapping metal scales sewn to cloth backing.

light.linothorax: Glued linen layers, stiff but flexible, Greek.
light.leather-chiton: Soft leather tunic with minimal reinforcement.

round-large.aspis: Deep bronze-faced wooden dish, ~90 cm, blazon centered.
round-large.viking-round: Flat wooden planks, radial paint, iron boss.

oval.thureos: Tall oval Celtic/Hellenistic shield, wooden planks, bronze spindle boss, painted triskele or knotwork.

rectangular.scutum: Curved oblong Roman body-shield, gold eagle + lightning blazon.

small.pelta: Crescent or small oval cavalry shield.

shields.none: Archers, two-handed swordsmen, elephants — no shield.

combinations: Helm crest color echoes the palette's ACCENT color (not primary).
Shield blazon uses the palette's HIGHLIGHT color on a primary-color field.
Light armor (linothorax, leather-chiton) pairs with pilos or attic helm — never corinthian.
Heavy armor (muscle-cuirass, lorica-segmentata, o-yoroi) always carries a matching crested helm.
Archers and two-handed swordsmen carry shield = none.
Cavalry (xyston lance) implies boeotian helm and pelta shield.
Muscle-cuirass implies corinthian or boeotian helm; lorica-segmentata is the exception (pairs with galea).
Gilded / ornate armor variants use a gold-primary palette; standard line variants use bronze or natural metal.
Transverse helm crest marks officers; fore-aft crest or no crest marks line troops.
Weapon-shield lock: doru pairs with aspis only; xyston pairs with pelta only — never cross these.

general: Positive framing only — never 'no X'. Rewrite 'no background' as 'isolated on dark gray grid'.
Specify materials, not adjectives: 'oxidized bronze muscle-cuirass' beats 'shiny armor'.
Keep a single cohesive style — do not mix 'flat vector' with 'photorealistic' or 'anime'.
For Leader cards, text on the art must be quoted literally and short (one name, one title).

nanoBananaPro.aspect: State aspect ratio in prose ('round 1:1 bust portrait', '3:4 TCG card').
nanoBananaPro.color: Prefer named/descriptive color ('woad blue, weathered bronze'). Hex codes are OK but not the strong lever.
nanoBananaPro.references: Up to 14 reference images with explicit role labels ('image 1 = style, image 2 = palette, image 3 = pose'). Strongest lever for house-style consistency.
nanoBananaPro.text: Quote literal strings and name the font. Finalize copy conversationally before requesting the image.
nanoBananaPro.avoid: Tag soup ('masterpiece, 4k, trending'). Negative prompts. Burying the subject under adjectives.

flux2Pro.structure: Single prose paragraph: Subject + Action + Style + Context, 30–80 words. Leading tokens weigh more — front-load the house style.
flux2Pro.aspect: Passed as width/height params (multiples of 16), NOT in the prompt text.
flux2Pro.color: Bind exact hex codes to specific objects: 'outline in #0B0B0B', 'shield field in #2F5A8A'. This is the strongest palette-lock lever.
flux2Pro.references: Up to 10 images, 9MP total budget across inputs + output.
flux2Pro.jsonPrompt: For catalog automation, Flux accepts a structured JSON prompt with scene/subjects/style/color_palette/lighting/camera keys.
flux2Pro.avoid: Negative prompts. Comma-separated tag lists. Style keywords buried at the end of a long paragraph. prompt_upsampling when determinism matters.

variationAxes.description: When a same-(culturalFamily, rarity) sibling already exists in sprites[], the generator must force the new sprite to differ on at least 3 of these 6 axes. This prevents clone output and widens the visual vocabulary of the catalog.

culturalFamilies.description: Cultures that share enough visual vocabulary to be treated as one cluster for collision detection. When picking a new sprite at a given rarity, the generator compares against every existing sprite whose culture maps to the same family here.

rarityLadder.description: One hero-lever per tier, clamp the others. At secret-rare and leader the composition DE-ESCALATES back toward iconic silhouette — the fix for the Pokémon SIR muddiness problem. The generator must emit exactly ONE loud axis per prompt and keep the calm axes calm.

uncommon.compositionAmbition: single-figure confident stance with a specialization-tell

rare.compositionAmbition: three-quarter dynamic, hero and environment cue

super-rare.compositionAmbition: narrative moment, hero-centered — NOT a crowd scene

secret-rare.compositionAmbition: iconic silhouette (DE-ESCALATED from super-rare), cinematic chiaroscuro

rarityLadder.deEscalationRule: At secret-rare and leader, the pose returns to a single iconic silhouette and supporting figures stay as darker silhouettes only. Never stack second-figure + kinetic-action + crowd at these tiers.

mtgSixFieldBrief.description: The semantic payload that feeds every model template. Modeled on MTG's art-brief structure (Muddy Colors, WotC Ultimate Masters). `Action` must contain a verb clause; `Mood` must be a one-sentence emotional punchline — not a list of adjectives. This is the strongest anti-generic lever.

fields.Setting: Who the subject is — culture, role, sub-archetype, age, gender, weapon, armor, helm, shield (the Subject line).
fields.Palette: Named colors for Nano, hex-bound colors for Flux. Include which palette slot gets the boost from the rarityLadder budget.
fields.Location: Where the subject is — background cue matched to the rarity (dark gray grid for common, silhouette for super-rare, painted scene for secret-rare/leader).
fields.Action: What the subject is DOING — a verb clause: 'bracing the shield wall', 'roaring and raising the dane-axe', 'scanning the ridgeline'. Never a static description.
fields.Focus: What the viewer's eye should land on first — usually the weapon tip, the crest color, the shield blazon, the gaze.
fields.Mood: A one-sentence emotional punchline. 'The line will hold, but barely.' 'He knows this is the last charge.' Not adjectives.

circleFrameLadder.description: The dark circular frame that contains the bust portrait is a first-class rarity signal. It escalates from a plain thin grey ring at common to a thick gemmed-and-runed ring at secret-rare, then DISSOLVES at leader (full-art bleed with gold-leaf nameplate instead). The ring must read as rarer at a glance than the previous tier — same philosophy as a TCG's card border. See each `rarities.<id>.circleFrame` for the full spec.
progression: common      — thin single-color dark-grey ring, plain, no ornament
uncommon    — thin gold hairline + four tiny dot accents at cardinal points
rare        — double gold line, engraved texture between lines, four small leaf corner motifs
super-rare  — thick ornate gold ring, continuous laurel-leaf scroll, four rosette bosses
secret-rare — thick ornate gold ring, embossed runes between ornaments, four gemmed corner bosses (sapphire/ruby/emerald/amethyst), prismatic sheen in the grooves
leader      — no ring at all; full-art edge-to-edge with a gold-leaf nameplate banner at the bottom
circleFrameLadder.rule: The circle frame is ALWAYS mentioned explicitly in the prompt. It is one of the fastest tier cues the eye reads — do not skip it.

hellenisticGuard.description: Special constraint: when culturalFamily is `hellenic` AND rarity is `super-rare` or higher, the generator must force at least TWO of these axes to differ from every existing hellenic super-rare+ sprite in sprites[]. This is the explicit fix for the current collision zone (spartan_royal_super_rare, athen_hoplite_elite_super_rare, companion_super_rare).
